intro: Copy and paste fonts are styled Unicode characters that look like different typefaces but travel as ordinary text, so they work in places that have no font menu: Instagram and TikTok bios, Discord and Roblox names, WhatsApp statuses, captions, comments and plain-text forms. Type once below to see the main families side by side, copy the one you want, and follow the links to a dedicated page when you need the full set for a single style.
copyBody: There is no font being copied. Each style is a separate alphabet inside Unicode — 𝓬𝓾𝓻𝓼𝓲𝓿𝓮 script, 𝗯𝗼𝗹𝗱 sans, 𝔤𝔬𝔱𝔥𝔦𝔠 Fraktur, ⓑⓤⓑⓑⓛⓔ circles, ꜱᴍᴀʟʟ ᴄᴀᴘꜱ — originally encoded for mathematics and phonetics and now used for decoration. When you press Copy, you get those characters, and any app that can show Unicode shows them in that shape. That is why these fonts survive where real formatting is stripped, and also why a rare character can show as a box on an old device.
popularTitle: Popular Copy and Paste Font Styles
popular: Cursive script (𝒴ℴ𝓊𝓇 𝒩𝒶𝓂ℯ) is the most searched, for names, signatures and soft bios. Bold sans (𝗬𝗼𝘂𝗿 𝗡𝗮𝗺𝗲) looks like native bold and is the safest everyday pick. Italic (𝑌𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑁𝑎𝑚𝑒) reads as a quote or tagline. Gothic Fraktur (𝔜𝔬𝔲𝔯 𝔑𝔞𝔪𝔢) is the heavy, old-school choice for gamer tags and dark aesthetics. Bubble (Ⓨⓞⓤⓡ) and small caps (Yᴏᴜʀ Nᴀᴍᴇ) are the playful and the tidy ends. Double-struck (𝕐𝕠𝕦𝕣) reads as outlined, monospace (𝚈𝚘𝚞𝚛) as code, and a sparkle or star frame finishes any of them.
steps: Enter a name, bio line, caption or short message. Digits convert in bold, double-struck and monospace; the script and italic alphabets cover letters only.
Use the chips to move between cursive, bold, italic, gothic, bubble and small styles. Each preset here is the lead style of a fuller page on this site.
Press Copy and paste into your app. Want more variations of one style — thirty cursive presets, every gothic frame? Open its dedicated page from the links below.
socialTitle: Fonts for Instagram, TikTok, Discord and More
social: Display names and bios are where these fonts get used most: Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Roblox, Snapchat, Twitch and LinkedIn all accept Unicode in the name and bio fields even though none of them has a font setting. Captions and comments accept them too; keep hashtags and links plain so they still work. Actual @usernames are restricted to letters, digits and underscores on nearly every platform, so the styled text belongs in the display name. Platform-specific pages for Instagram, TikTok and Discord cover each app's quirks and character limits.
limitNote: screen readers announce these characters as mathematical symbols rather than as words, so keep essential information in ordinary text as well.
specificTitle: Pasted Fonts vs Downloadable Font Files
specific: A font file (TTF, OTF, WOFF) changes how a device draws ordinary letters, which is what you want for a document, a website or a print design. Copy and paste fonts change the letters themselves, which is what you want when the destination has no font menu. The two do not mix: a copied Unicode word will not become plain text in Word, and a downloaded font cannot be pasted into an Instagram bio. Use this page and its sub-pages for the second case; for the first, use a licensed typeface in your design app.

Bold, italic, serif and small: the bold font generator covers every weight, italic covers slanted serif and sans, the serif page covers editorial styles, and the small text generator covers small caps, superscript and subscript. Blockletter and monospace handle heavy capitals and typewriter spacing.

Decorative and themed: gothic and old English for blackletter, bubble for circled letters, aesthetic and cute for soft styles, y2k and brat for era looks, stylish and cool for understated profile text, and fancy text for the complete catalogue of 300+ presets. Platform pages — Instagram, TikTok, Discord, Roblox — tune the same characters to one app's fields. Every one of those pages uses the same copy-and-paste mechanism as the generator above; the difference is depth and framing.

faqs: What are copy and paste fonts?

Styled Unicode characters that look like different typefaces — cursive, bold, gothic, bubble — but are ordinary text, so they can be pasted into any field that accepts Unicode, including bios and names with no font setting.
Are these fonts free to use?
Yes. This generator and every style page on the site are free, with no account, download or usage limit, and the characters themselves are part of the Unicode Standard.
Why does my pasted text show boxes or question marks?

The device or app has no glyph for that character. Bold sans, cursive and small caps are supported almost everywhere; rarer styles may fail on older devices. Switch to a plainer style with the same text.
Can I use these fonts in my username?
Usually only in the display name and bio. Most platforms restrict the @handle to plain letters, digits and underscores.
Do these fonts work in Word or Google Docs?
They paste in, but as the same Unicode characters, not as a font you can change. For documents, install a real font instead and keep the text plain.
Are these fonts searchable or readable by screen readers?
No. Search treats styled characters as different from plain letters, and screen readers announce them as symbols. Use them for decoration and keep essential text plain.
Which style should I pick for a name?
Bold sans for legibility, cursive for a soft or personal feel, gothic for a heavy gamer look, small caps for a tidy bio. Preview your exact name — some styles suit short names better than long ones.
